_note: THE NOTIFICATION PERMISSION LADDER (parity/F02-notifications.md §3a `permission`/`status`). Two things every notification stack gets wrong are pinned here. (1) PROVISIONAL AUTHORIZATION: iOS will deliver quietly, to the notification centre, with NO PROMPT AT ALL, and will then offer the user a Keep/Turn-off choice on the first notification they actually see. It is the highest-conversion path in mobile and almost nobody ships it, because it is one option constant buried in a bitmask. Here it is one flag, and the escalation from provisional to full is a real transition with its own rule. (2) THE SETTINGS TRANSITION: a user turns notifications off in Settings while the app is backgrounded, and a module that trusts its cached status prompts into a void forever. The OS reading always wins, and that is a function, not a comment.
_note_options: The option vocabulary, exact case. `provisional` is an option like the rest so that quiet authorization is one flag rather than a second API.
_note_support: What each platform can honour. An option this platform cannot honour is DROPPED and REPORTED, never silently discarded: an app that asked for critical alerts and got ordinary ones has to be able to find that out.
_note_android: POST_NOTIFICATIONS is a runtime permission from API 33. BELOW 33 THERE IS NOTHING TO ASK: the module answers granted with prompted:false rather than pretending to show a dialog. A user who turned the app's notifications off in system settings still reads as denied on any API level, and there the honest answer is a refusal pointing at Settings, because no in-app dialog can undo it.

_note_apply: Folding the OS's answer back. A DECLINED ESCALATION IS NOT A LOST GRANT: an app that was delivering quietly and asked for more must still be delivering quietly afterwards. A naive `granted ? granted : denied` throws away a working feature to record the refusal of a different one, and the user never sees another notification.

_note_observe: THE SETTINGS-CHANGED-WHILE-BACKGROUNDED TRANSITION. Every one of these happens outside the app, and the only correct response is to believe the OS. `broadcast` is true exactly when the status actually moved, so a resume that changed nothing is silent - a permission event on every foreground is noise nobody can act on.

_note_sequence: The whole ladder as one run, because the individual transitions above can each be right while the composition is wrong. AFTER A SETTINGS DENIAL THE NEXT permission() CALL MUST REFUSE - that is the bug this sequence exists to catch, and it is invisible to any test that only checks one transition.
